validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, and its history is unusually well attested for an occupied-territory line. (1) An institutional source independent of gem.wiki — a Wayback-archived page (snapshot 2022-06-08, matching the wiki's own 'accessed 2019-10-28' citation) belonging to VNIPItransgaz, the Soviet/Russian gas-trunkline design institute — lists 'Rostov-Taganrog-Zhdanov' by that exact name in its table of major magistral (trunk) gas pipelines it helped design: diameter 400-1000mm, pressure 5.4 MPa, length 516km, 1 thread, Russia+Ukraine. This matches the wiki page title verbatim and the sheet's Length (516km) and Diameter (1000mm, the range's upper bound) exactly. (2) Multiple Russian-origin sources (RIA Novosti 2014-10-22, neftegaz.ru 2014) independently describe a 'Taganrog-Mariupol' gas pipeline as a real Soviet-built (1950s) line that supplied southern Donetsk-region industry at 350,000 m3/hour until it was shut down in 2009 amid the Russia-Ukraine gas conflict — consistent with the sheet's current Status=retired as a description of that 2009-2022 dormant period. (3) Kommersant (2022-07-13, kommersant.ru/doc/5459063), a major Russian business daily, independently confirms this is a real, named 'Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk' Soviet-era pipeline whose Ukrainian section 'was not used after the 2009 gas conflict' and reports that as of July 2022 gas already reaches Berdyansk via this route, with Russia's Energy Ministry (tasked by Deputy PM Marat Khusnullin) and occupation governor Yevgeniy Balitsky discussing its restoration/extension. (4) mariupol-news.ru (2023-09-04, Donbassgaz/Telegram-sourced) reports completed reconstruction of Mariupol's GRS-1 gas distribution station, explicitly named as fed 'from the magistral gas pipeline Taganrog-Mariupol', with 150,000 m3/hour new equipment capacity. (5) United24 Media (2025-07-24, Ukrainian, independent of the Russian-origin cluster, citing the Ukrainian Center of Journalistic Investigations) independently corroborates that Russia is building/has built pipelines 'from Taganrog...to the occupied Mariupol, and another continuing to Berdyansk, with Melitopol as the final destination', as part of tripling capacity on the Rostov-Crimea land-corridor gas supply. So: this is not a GEM-only or wiki-only entity — it is a real, historically documented Soviet trunk that has been the subject of active, multiply-sourced Russian reconstruction/extension activity since 2022, corroborated by an independent Ukrainian outlet. Two leads cited on the wiki page itself (tsoua.com/key-facts, a LinkedIn company page) are generic aggregate pages that never name this pipeline and were correctly not usable as refs for it. CLASSIFICATION: correct — every non-GEM source above describes it as a magistral/trunk transmission gas pipeline (not a gathering or process line); PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas both confirmed. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 6-pipeline in-scope roster (P0761 Soyuz/Orenburg, P0788 Ostrogozhsk-Shebelinka/Kharkiv, P0793 Stavropol-Moscow, P1487 Poland-Ukraine/Hermanowice, P1773 Romania-Ukraine/Khotyn) — none overlap geographically or by name with the Rostov/Taganrog-Azov-coast corridor; no duplicate found. Note for the record (not a duplicate — a distinct, shorter, non-roster asset worth knowing about): Kommersant explicitly distinguishes the OLD Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk trunk (this row) from a separate NEW 'Berdyansk-Melitopol' extension (over 100km, first proposed July 2022) that United24 (2025) suggests is still under active construction — that Berdyansk-Melitopol segment is not P1457 and is not in this batch's roster; flagging only so a future discovery pass knows it exists.

validity.recommendation: verify whether Length=516km is consistent with StartLocation=Taganrog — the only source for 516km (VNIPItransgaz) explicitly names the FULL 'Rostov-Taganrog-Zhdanov' corridor (i.e. it includes the Rostov->Taganrog segment upstream of the sheet's own Start point); if the row is meant to track only Taganrog->Berdyansk/Zhdanov(Mariupol), the true length is shorter than 516km and either Length should be trimmed or StartLocation corrected to Rostov to match the sourced figure and the wiki page's own title
validity.researcher_notes: The one independent length/diameter source I found (the archived VNIPItransgaz trunk-pipeline table) states 516km / 400-1000mm for the pipeline named 'Rostov-Taganrog-Zhdanov' — i.e. Rostov as the actual start point, not Taganrog. GEM's own StartLocation for this row is 'Taganrog' (Rostov is not mentioned anywhere in the sheet's location fields), yet the Length value (516.00km) matches the Rostov-anchored figure exactly. I searched specifically for a length figure for just the 'Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk' leg (i.e. excluding the Rostov->Taganrog upstream segment) and could not find one independently — the closest hit ('more than 100km') turned out on closer reading of the source Kommersant article to describe the NEW Berdyansk-Melitopol extension, not this pipeline. So I cannot independently confirm the 516km figure is correct for a Taganrog-only start point; it may be correct only if the true start is Rostov (matching the wiki title) or if the Taganrog->Berdyansk leg genuinely runs ~516km along the Azov coast (plausible given Rostov-Taganrog is itself a comparatively short ~70km hop, leaving most of the 516km for the Taganrog-onward run, but I have no source stating this explicitly). Diameter=1000mm is the source range's upper bound (400-1000mm along the line's length) — reasonable as a 'primary/max diameter' convention but worth noting the pipe narrows toward its far (likely Ukrainian) end, which may matter if this row is ever segmented.

validity.recommendation: keep the Gazprom/TSOU cross-border split for now, but flag that on-the-ground operation of the Ukrainian/occupied section since 2022 appears to run through Donbassgaz (a DNR-linked entity), not TSOU — worth revisiting when the country's occupied-asset ownership convention is settled
validity.researcher_notes: Owner1=Gazprom PJSC / Owner2=Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine (TSOU) follows the country guidance's correct cross-border convention (Gazprom for the Russian section, the Ukrainian state entity for the Ukrainian section) rather than the flagged error pattern of Gazprom claiming 100% of a wholly-Ukrainian row — this pipeline genuinely starts in Russia (Taganrog, Rostov Oblast). A single 2014 Russian trade-press source (neftegaz.ru) directly names Gazprom as owner of the 'Taganrog-Mariupol' line. However, I found no source — for either 2014 or 2022-2025 — that names TSOU in connection with this specific pipeline; the wiki-cited TSOU/LinkedIn pages are generic corporate pages that never mention it. More importantly, the entity actually doing reconstruction/distribution work on the Ukrainian end since 2022 is Donbassgaz (per mariupol-news.ru 2023-09-04, a DNR-based gas company, working under Russian officials Khusnullin/Solntsev), not TSOU — consistent with TSOU having no practical operational control over Russian-occupied Mariupol/Zaporizhzhia Oblast since 2022. I am not proposing to remove TSOU (it remains the de jure Ukrainian operator of the national GTS, and GEM elsewhere keeps de jure Ukrainian ownership on occupied assets), just flagging that de facto control has moved to Donbassgaz and no source specifically pairs TSOU with this row.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The recorded Status='retired' (LastUpdated 2023-09-11) describes only the pipeline's 2009-2022 dormant period and is now stale: this line has been under active restoration/rebuild since mid-2022, well before the sheet's own last-update date. Timeline found: (1) Kommersant, 2022-07-13 — 'Ukrainian section' of the old Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk pipeline 'was not used after the 2009 gas conflict' but 'gas currently reaches Berdyansk from this direction' as of that date, and Russia's Energy Ministry/occupation governor Balitsky were actively working a restoration/extension plan (targeting completion in ~1.5 months, i.e. ~Sept 2022). (2) mariupol-news.ru, 2023-09-04 — reconstruction of the Mariupol GRS-1 station fed 'from the magistral gas pipeline Taganrog-Mariupol' is reported COMPLETE, with 150,000 m3/hour of new equipment, i.e. gas actively entering Mariupol's distribution network via this line as of that date. (3) United24 Media, 2025-07-24, citing the Ukrainian Center of Journalistic Investigations and 2024-dated video evidence — independently (this is the Ukrainian/non-Russian-origin corroborating leg) confirms Russia has been building pipelines on this exact Taganrog->Mariupol->Berdyansk axis as part of an ongoing land-corridor gas buildout, still described as under construction/expansion as recently as mid-2025. A DNR Minstroy order dated 2025-03-27 (approving planning documentation for 'capital repair of a linear object') looked like further corroboration but the domain (minstroy-dnr.ru) now 301-redirects to an unrelated site (gazetakursk.ru) — dead/repurposed, NOT cited, and the RBC 2022-10-25 report of DNR-sourced gas reaching Zaporizhzhia-Oblast settlements could not be verified (401, no Wayback snapshot) so is also not cited, though it is directionally consistent. Net read: 'retired' is wrong for the 2022-2025 period; the safest characterization given ongoing capital-repair/construction activity confirmed as recently as 2025 (rather than confirmed full-corridor commercial operation) is 'construction', even though the Mariupol-supplying sub-segment has apparently been delivering gas since ~2023. Tier held at medium rather than high per the country's occupied-territory rule (Russian-state/occupation-administration-linked sources — Kommersant, mariupol-news.ru/Donbassgaz — count as one origin; United24 is the second, independent, origin, but its corroboration is general/directional rather than a precise operational-status confirmation). Flagging for Update to decide between 'construction' (my recommendation, reflecting the still-incomplete Berdyansk/Melitopol extension) and 'operating' (defensible if the intent is to describe the Mariupol-supplying leg specifically, which has evidence of gas delivery since 2023) — either way, 'retired' should not stand.

summary: P1457 (Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk): existence/classification/no-duplicate confirmed via non-wiki Russian+Ukrainian sources; STATUS FLAGGED STALE — recorded 'retired' describes only the 2009-2022 dormant period, but multiple sources (Kommersant 2022-07, mariupol-news.ru 2023-09, United24 2025-07) show active Russian restoration/construction and at least partial gas delivery to Mariupol since 2023, so verdict=change to proposed_status='construction' (tier medium, occupied-territory sourcing); refs added for Length/Diameter/Location/Fuel/PipelineType/Owner1(Gazprom); flagged spec concern that the sourced 516km figure is anchored to a Rostov (not Taganrog) start point, and attribution caveat that Owner2=TSOU is unsupported for this row and Donbassgaz appears to be the de-facto operator since 2022; no UNRESOLVED fills beyond the noted Owner2 gap.
